messages:
samira: bringing up a recurring onboarding support case — customers see "SSE parse error" with no extra context and get stuck in the demo. They send screenshots of the UI spinner and we have almost no telemetry to explain why.

ben: do we have logs from the sampleapp when debug enabled? most people don't turn it on so we miss the low-level churn.

samira: i turned on verbose locally and reproduced. The stream doesn't error; it's a sequence of 26 tiny `data:` frames (5-12 bytes) then a connection close. Our SDK surfaces a generic "parse error" because final JSON.parse fails (partial buffer). No metric flagged that we saw lots of tiny fragments.

ivy: can you paste the raw bytes? even a hex-like dump helps.

samira: pasted from tcpdump: ```
64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 63 68 6f 69 63 65 73 22 3a 5b 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 22 68 65
6c 22 7d 5d 7d 0a
64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 64 65 6c 74 61 22 3a 22 6c 6f 22 7d 0a 0a
```
 — notice the first chunk ends mid-token and the LB chops several tiny pieces.

ben: this is useful. Suggestion: SDK should add an opt-in `sse.debug` that logs per-chunk size/hex, and a higher-level heuristic that detects "fragment storm" (N small chunks within T ms) and annotates logs/telemetry. That would let support quickly see proxy-induced resegmentation.

ivy: +1. Also add a user-facing hint in sampleapp when we detect this pattern: show a small banner "Network proxy may be truncating streaming responses — try running sampleapp locally or enabling SSE debug logs" with a link to troubleshooting. Saves 20min per ticket.

ben: telemetry: emit events `sse.fragment_count`, `sse.avg_chunk_bytes`, `sse.eof_unflushed` and tag with sdk_version + route. Add alert rule if avg_chunk_bytes < 16 and fragment_count > 10 within a 3s window.

samira: love it. For the parser itself: keep EOF-as-flush behavior, but additionally treat long sequences of small chunks as suspicious and trigger idle-flush sooner (config override). We can expose `sse.idle_flush_ms` as before but also auto-lower it when fragment-storm detected.

ivy: keep debug logs verbose but gated behind `sse.debug=true` env var. They should include per-chunk: timestamp, size, hex prefix (first 40 bytes), and a short hint if heuristic matches. Example line: `SSE-CHUNK t=162: size=9 hex=646174613a20... hint=mid-token`

ben: will add a lightweight library function to create a deterministic short hash of the chunk so we can dedupe repeated retransmits without storing entire payload in logs. Only record full hex for debug mode.

telemetry-bot: created metric(s): sse.fragment_count, sse.avg_chunk_bytes, sse.eof_unflushed. Dashboard stub created under "Redwood / SDK / SSE Diagnostics".

samira: i'll draft the sampleapp UI hint and short README blurb with reproduction steps (curl + `--no-buffer` vs proxy). Also add a troubleshooting checklist: (1) enable sse.debug, (2) check fragment_count & avg_chunk_bytes, (3) run sampleapp locally to rule out proxy, (4) toggle idle_flush_ms.

devx-bot: CI kicked off for branch feature/sse-diagnostics. Tests: unit + small integ with mitmproxy that simulates fragment storm.

ben: once merged let's ship a tiny patch release and update the onboarding guide with the banner screenshot and the debug env var. Ops has an internal KB for common proxy appliances too.

samira: thanks all. this should cut down support ping time a lot.

devx-bot: merged to main after green CI. Release note: "SDKs: optional SSE debug tracing and diagnostics heuristics (fragment-count, avg-chunk-bytes, eof-unflushed) + sampleapp UI hint for proxy-induced fragmentation; exposes sse.debug and sse.idle_flush_ms for troubleshooting."
